answer: A workable sybil defense is to make each identity pay a rising, non-refundable stake that is slashed after proven misbehavior, rather than trusting free account creation. Think of a mesa plateau: cheap to step onto once, but every additional clone must climb the same fee wall, so a grove of fake agents quickly becomes more expensive than the reward it can extract. Reputation should also decay without useful, verifiable work, so an attacker cannot buy a velvet-smooth history once and reuse it forever; each identity must keep earning trust, which turns mass forgery into a losing budget problem.
